{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nc-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f4ca59225b5866bd59c995d56338505c3b6c5ea71e8548db89fc618350e26c6b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nc-class-c:lineage:28","source_registry_sha256":"e128656a3d00ba5437556728ebd87f5842c83601163739613417fe77cf9f423b","source_liveness_sha256":"dbfdf3e6d892a41c42c05809a9213d44a78aedd480dc6de23937c97292428b74"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Pedestrians, school buses, emergency vehicles and police stops","heading":"C — Pedestrians, motorcyclists, school buses, emergency vehicles, move-over, law-enforcement stops and farm equipment (North Carolina)","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Pedestrians, motorcyclists, school buses, emergency vehicles, move-over, law-enforcement stops and farm equipment (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: who has the right of way when people on foot, school buses and emergency vehicles are involved, how to behave during a traffic stop, and how to share the road with slow farm machinery.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
The pickup-bed rule for children does not apply when a supervising adult rides in the bed, in an emergency, in a parade, or while the vehicle serves an agricultural enterprise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Breaking the pickup-bed rule brings a ticket and a $25 fine; it is an infraction with no court costs, license points or insurance surcharge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
A parked car in the sun can get roughly 40 to 50 degrees hotter inside than outside, even with a window cracked, so leaving children or animals inside can cause heat stroke or death. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
In winter, snow blocking the exhaust pipe while the car warms up can force carbon monoxide inside; the gas cannot be seen, smelled or tasted but is poisonous. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
At an intersection with no traffic signals, pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, or in an unmarked one formed by extending the sidewalk lines, have the right of way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Where ordinary signals control an intersection, pedestrians follow the same signals as drivers going their direction and should not begin crossing on red or yellow. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian crossing on a green signal has the right of way over every vehicle, including one turning across the pedestrian's path. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
If the light turns yellow or red while a pedestrian is still in the street, drivers must let that person finish crossing safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
At an unsignaled intersection the law gives special consideration to a blind pedestrian who holds out a white cane, a red-tipped white cane, or has a guide dog. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
Where Walk and Don't Walk signals operate, pedestrians obey them instead of the regular lights, and crossing on Walk gives them the same right of way as a green light. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
If you are going through on green and a pedestrian steps into your path against a red signal, warn them with your horn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A02
The law requires a horn warning whenever a turn, stop or start from a parked spot may affect a pedestrian, and if the pedestrian keeps going the driver must stop; yield even when the pedestrian is not entitled to it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A02
A driver who fails to signal properly and forces a motorcycle to change lanes or leave the road will be charged and fined, and the same applies if a crash with damage or injury results. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A02
A school bus may travel no faster than 45 mph. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A02
Be especially careful during school bus hours, generally 7 to 9 a.m. and 2 to 4 p.m. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A02
When a school bus shows its mechanical stop arm or flashing red lights to load or unload, approaching drivers must stop and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn, the lights go off and the bus begins moving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus that stops for passengers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A03
Police cars, ambulances, fire engines and rescue vehicles using flashing lights and sirens always have the right of way. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A03
When an emergency vehicle approaches from ahead or behind, pull to the right-hand curb or edge and stop completely, staying there until it passes or an officer waves you on. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A03
Do not park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle stopped at a crash or giving assistance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A03
Stay at least one block away from fire trucks answering an alarm, and never drive over a fire hose. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A03
Every vehicle must yield to an approaching emergency vehicle, except traffic going the opposite way on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A03
On a road of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, only the traffic behind a stopped school bus has to stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A03
On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only traffic following the school bus must stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A03
On a two-lane road with a center turning lane, all traffic in both directions stops for the school bus. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A03
On a four-lane road with no median separation, all traffic in both directions stops for the school bus. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A04
Move-over law: when an authorized emergency or public service vehicle with warning lights on is parked within 12 feet of the road and you have two or more lanes your way, change out of the lane closest to it and stay out until clear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A04
If you have only one lane in your direction, slow down and keep a reduced, safe speed until you are fully past the stopped emergency vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A04
When police lights or a siren appear behind you, stay calm, signal, and pull to the right off the travel lanes at the nearest safe spot. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A04
With no safe place to stop right away, switch on your four-way flashers and slow by about 10 mph to show the officer you know, then drive lawfully to the nearest safe area. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A04
If you honestly doubt that an unmarked car is real police, you may call 911 before pulling over and give your name and location to confirm the stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A04
Once stopped, shift to Park, lower the window, turn off the engine and silence devices; everyone stays seated, and you keep your seat belt on unless the officer asks otherwise. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A05
Keep both hands on the steering wheel, have passengers keep their hands visible, and have back-seat riders rest their hands on the front seatback. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A05
State law requires you to identify yourself and hand over your license and vehicle registration; after that you may decide whether to answer further questions. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A05
Never reach for a weapon during a stop; a weapon must be in plain view or locked away unless there is a proper permit, and a concealed weapon permit holder must tell the officer a weapon is in the vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A05
Do not get out, or let passengers get out, unless told to, and do not dig under seats or in the glove box for documents unless the officer asks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A05
Signing a traffic ticket does not admit guilt; argue your side in court rather than at the roadside. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A05
Resisting, delaying or obstructing an officer during a traffic stop is a class 2 misdemeanor. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A06
If you believe an officer behaved improperly, write down what happened and report it promptly to the officer's agency, whose name appears on the ticket. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A06
Most crashes with farm equipment happen on clear days, in daylight, on dry paved roads, and they are usually sideswipes or angle crashes. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A06
These crashes often happen when farm machinery slows to turn left and a following driver tries to pass, sometimes after mistaking the operator's left-hand signal for a wave to pass. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A06
Passing farm equipment in a no-passing zone is illegal, and the machine may be wider than it looks from behind. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F43 | anchor: A06
The only advisable time to pass farm equipment on a public road is when the operator pulls off at a practical spot to let traffic by. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-F44 | anchor: A06
Farm equipment must show one white light in front and a red light at the rear visible for up to 500 feet, or two red reflectors at least four inches across in place of that rear light. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0053]

Misconceptions: on a road with a center turning lane but only two lanes, both directions still stop for a school bus; only a median or a wider road with a turning lane frees oncoming traffic; a pedestrian crossing on green beats a turning car; the move-over rule applies to parked public service vehicles too, not only police; signing a ticket is not a confession; a farm operator's left-hand signal can mean the machine is about to turn left, not that you may pass.
Mnemonics: median or many lanes with a middle turn lane, only followers halt; lights on a shoulder, move over or slow down.
Glossary: crosswalk means a marked or implied pedestrian crossing at an intersection; mechanical stop signal means the stop arm a school bus extends; move-over law means the duty to change lanes or slow near a stopped emergency or service vehicle; limited-access highway means a road entered only at interchanges; infraction means a noncriminal violation.
Dynamic facts: school bus hours are typical times rather than fixed rules, and traffic-stop procedures and fines can change by statute; confirm current law.
